title: repro-checksum-catalog-backtrack-plan for quant profiles (FP8/INT8)
creator: Ava Chen
description: Establish a deterministic artifact catalog and backtrack (rollback) plan for quantization profiles covering FP8 and INT8 calibration outputs. Deliverables: canonical serialization for profiles, stable hashing/signing scheme, an indexable artifact registry, CI validation gates, and an operator-safe rollback CLI/API path.
background: We routinely generate per-model quantization artifacts (per-layer scale/zero-point, clipping params, per-channel stats) for FP8 and INT8 calibration runs. Currently artifacts are generated by multiple calibration harnesses with small structural differences (ordering, optional fields) that make bytewise reproducibility impossible and complicate rollback and audit. Several incidents in the past 6 months showed ambiguity when comparing artifacts during regression detection and when reverting a model rollout to a previous quant profile.
proposed_solution: 1) Define a canonical JSON/CBOR serialization schema for quant profiles and calibration snapshots (strict field ordering, explicit nulls, canonical numeric formats). 2) Adopt BLAKE3-256 as the canonical artifact digest. 3) Produce a signed manifest per artifact: manifest contains artifact digest, model checkpoint tag, tokenizer hash, dataset digest, calibration harness version, seeds, and hyperparameters. 4) Store artifacts and manifests in the quant-artifacts registry with immutable object IDs and index entries. 5) Add CI steps to validate canonicalization and digest stability across harness versions. 6) Expose a safe operator path (quantctl restore --artifact-hash) to backtrack runtime routes and rollout mapping in Console.
decisions: - Hash algorithm: BLAKE3-256 chosen for speed and resistance to accidental collisions; why not SHA256: BLAKE3 faster for large per-layer blobs and has streaming support. - Signature scheme: ECDSA P-256 with KMS-backed signing keys (customer-managed KMS option later). - Serialization: use CBOR for on-disk storage but keep human-readable canonical JSON for diffs; both derived from the same canonical schema and ordering rules. - Include RNG seeds and calibration tool git SHA in manifest to make calibration replayable.
tradeoffs: - CBOR binary saves space and is faster to hash but is less human-friendly for debugging. Solution: store both CBOR (primary) and canonical JSON (secondary) for each artifact. - Adding more metadata increases manifest size but improves traceability. We'll keep the manifest bounded by only including fields needed for replay + audit. - Signing every artifact adds latency; signing happens asynchronously after artifact commit to registry and will not block serving rollouts.
test_plan: - Regression CI job that runs the canonicalizer on the existing golden calibration suites and verifies digest equality across multiple runs. - Cross-harness consistency tests: run FP8 calibration in both harness A and harness B with identical seeds and verify canonicalized manifest hashes match. - End-to-end acceptance: create a canary rollout that switches to a quant profile, run a smoke eval suite, then use quantctl restore to backtrack; validate that the restored routing matches the previous profile and that metrics roll back to canary baseline within thresholds.
test_matrix: - Models: 3 sizes (small/medium/large) across GPT-style and encoder-decoder. - Quant modes: FP8 per-channel, FP8 per-tensor, INT8 symmetric, INT8 asymmetric. - Datasets: calibration-set-v1, calibration-set-v2 (different tokenization). - CI scenarios: deterministic seed replay, harness-version mismatch detection, manifest tamper detection.

Implement canonicalizer library (python + rust bindings) that outputs CBOR and stable JSON
Integrate BLAKE3-256 digest and signing into calibration pipeline
Extend quant-artifacts registry API to store manifest + secondary JSON and expose /v1/quant/artifacts endpoints
Add CI validations and goldenset comparisons
Build quantctl CLI commands: publish, list, verify, restore
Console integration: add artifact-level metadata to rollout UI and a 'revert to artifact' action
Write operator runbook and run internal tabletop exercise
rollout_plan: Phase 1: internal-only - publish artifacts from current harness and run CI validation on goldensets. Phase 2: opt-in lab clusters - allow specific teams to reference artifacts via registry and use quantctl restore in staging. Phase 3: default for new calibration outputs - enforced canonicalization at artifact publish time. Phase 4: governance: enable signed-manifest verification in Dedicated and Private runtimes as a policy toggle.
rollback_playbook: - Preconditions: operator has artifact-hash to restore and RBAC for artifact restore. - Steps: 1) quantctl verify --hash <H>; 2) quantctl restore --hash <H> --target <route>; 3) Console creates rollback rollout linked to artifact H and triggers canary; 4) Monitor eval-suites and latency/cost; 5) If regressions persist, run quantctl rollback --route <route> to previous artifact or orchestrate partial traffic shift. - Post-incident: run artifacts diff (canonical JSON) and attach to incident report; if tampering or inconsistency detected, rotate signing key and mark affected artifacts as deprecated.
acceptance_criteria: - Canonicalizer produces identical digest for repeated runs with same inputs (verified by CI). - Cross-harness identical calibration runs (same seeds) produce identical manifests and digests. - Operator restore path successfully re-maps routing and the runtime reports the restored artifact hash in its metrics and trace logs. - Audit logs show manifest signature verification for published artifacts. - Documentation and runbook reviewed by SRE and Security.
notes: - For calibration numeric stability, we will normalize floating values to 8 decimal places in canonical JSON; CBOR stores full float value but canonicalizer rounds before computing manifest fields used in digest. - We should consider adding a small provenance header that includes human-readable calibration notes (reason for run, PR link). - We should coordinate with Desktop Console team to add artifact filters in the Rollouts page.
